source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בִּלְעָם֙ אֶל־בָּלָ֔ק בְּנֵה־לִ֥י בָזֶ֖ה שִׁבְעָ֣ה מִזְבְּחֹ֑ת וְהָכֵ֥ן לִי֙ בָּזֶ֔ה שִׁבְעָ֥ה פָרִ֖ים וְשִׁבְעָ֥ה אֵילִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Balaam to Balak, build for me in this [place] seven altars, and prepare for me in this [place] seven bulls and seven rams.

en.L: And Balaam said to Balak, "Build for me here seven altars, and prepare for me here seven bulls and seven rams."
en.B: Balaam said to Balak, "Build me seven altars here, and get seven bulls and seven rams ready for me here."
en.R: Balaam told Balak, "Build seven altars for me here. Then get seven bulls and seven rams ready for me."

es.L: Y dijo Balaam a Balac: «Constrúyeme aquí siete altares, y prepárame aquí siete novillos y siete carneros».
es.B: Balaam dijo a Balac: «Edifícame aquí siete altares, y tenme preparados aquí siete novillos y siete carneros».
es.R: Balaam le dijo a Balac: «Construye aquí siete altares para mí. Luego prepárame siete novillos y siete carneros».

fr.L: Et Balaam dit à Balak : « Bâtis-moi ici sept autels, et prépare-moi ici sept taureaux et sept béliers. »
fr.B: Balaam dit à Balak : « Construis-moi ici sept autels, et tiens prêts pour moi, ici même, sept taureaux et sept béliers. »
fr.R: Balaam a dit à Balak : « Construis sept autels pour moi ici. Ensuite, prépare-moi sept taureaux et sept béliers. »

sw.L: Kisha Balaamu akamwambia Balaki, "Nijengee hapa madhabahu saba, na uniandalie hapa mafahali saba na kondoo dume saba."
sw.B: Balaamu alimwambia Balaki, "Nijengee madhabahu saba hapa, na uniwekee tayari hapa mafahali saba na kondoo dume saba."
sw.R: Balaamu alimwambia Balaki, "Nijengee madhabahu saba hapa. Kisha uniandalie mafahali saba na kondoo dume saba."

decisions.choice: Balaam: a diviner from Aram hired by Balak, king of Moab, to curse Israel
decisions.reason: Balak had sent for Balaam from Pethor on the Euphrates and offered him rich payment to curse Israel (22:5-7, 17). God had told Balaam he could speak only the word God gave him (22:20, 35, 38). This chapter tells of his first two attempts.

decisions.choice: seven altars, seven bulls, seven rams: a full and costly rite before seeking a word from God
decisions.reason: Seven was the number of fullness. A large offering on seven altars was meant to win the favor of the god being approached before an oracle was sought; 24:1 says that on these occasions Balaam had gone to look for omens. He calls for the same rite again in verses 14 and 29.

decisions.choice: here
decisions.reason: "In this [place]" is the ordinary way to say "here". Readable says it once, since both commands are about the same place.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("dit", "offrirent"); passé composé at Readable ("a dit", "ont offert")
decisions.reason: As in the rest of the Pentateuch: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative, the passé composé that of spoken and school French. The oracles themselves are speech and keep the tenses of speech.

source.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ בָּלָ֔ק כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֣ר בִּלְעָ֑ם וַיַּ֨עַל בָּלָ֧ק וּבִלְעָ֛ם פָּ֥ר וָאַ֖יִל בַּמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And did Balak just as had spoken Balaam, and offered up Balak and Balaam a bull and a ram on the altar.

en.L: And Balak did just as Balaam had spoken, and Balak and Balaam offered up a bull and a ram on [each] altar.
en.B: Balak did as Balaam said, and Balak and Balaam offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
en.R: Balak did what Balaam said. Then the two of them offered a bull and a ram on each altar.

es.L: E hizo Balac tal como había dicho Balaam, y ofrecieron Balac y Balaam un novillo y un carnero sobre [cada] altar.
es.B: Balac hizo lo que Balaam le dijo, y Balac y Balaam ofrecieron un novillo y un carnero en cada altar.
es.R: Balac hizo lo que Balaam le pidió. Luego los dos ofrecieron un novillo y un carnero en cada altar.

fr.L: Et Balak fit comme Balaam avait dit, et Balak et Balaam offrirent un taureau et un bélier sur [chaque] autel.
fr.B: Balak fit ce que Balaam avait demandé, et Balak et Balaam offrirent sur chaque autel un taureau et un bélier.
fr.R: Balak a fait ce que Balaam avait dit. Puis les deux hommes ont offert un taureau et un bélier sur chaque autel.

sw.L: Naye Balaki akafanya kama Balaamu alivyosema, na Balaki na Balaamu wakatoa fahali mmoja na kondoo dume mmoja juu ya [kila] madhabahu.
sw.B: Balaki alifanya kama Balaamu alivyosema, na Balaki na Balaamu wakatoa fahali na kondoo dume juu ya kila madhabahu.
sw.R: Balaki alifanya kama Balaamu alivyosema. Kisha wote wawili wakatoa fahali mmoja na kondoo dume mmoja juu ya kila madhabahu.

decisions.choice: on the altar: on each of the seven altars
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "on the altar" in the singular, but seven bulls and seven rams were made ready for seven altars (verse 1), so one bull and one ram went on each. Verse 4 says the same.

decisions.choice: offered up: burnt offerings, burned whole on the altar
decisions.reason: The verb means to make an offering go up, the word used for burnt offerings, which were burned whole so that the smoke went up. Verse 3 calls them Balak's burnt offering.

decisions.choice: [each] altar
decisions.reason: Literal adds "each" in brackets so that the reader does not picture one altar only (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר בִּלְעָ֜ם לְבָלָ֗ק הִתְיַצֵּב֮ עַל־עֹלָתֶךָ֒ וְאֵֽלְכָ֗ה אוּלַ֞י יִקָּרֵ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לִקְרָאתִ֔י וּדְבַ֥ר מַה־יַּרְאֵ֖נִי וְהִגַּ֣דְתִּי לָ֑ךְ וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ שֶֽׁפִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Balaam to Balak, station yourself beside your burnt offering, and let me go; perhaps will come Yahweh to meet me, and [the] word of whatever he shows me I will tell to you. And he went [to a] bare height.

en.L: And Balaam said to Balak, "Station yourself beside your burnt offering, and let me go. Perhaps {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will come to meet me, and whatever word {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shows me I will tell you." And he went to a bare height.
en.B: Then Balaam said to Balak, "Stay here beside your burnt offering while I go. Perhaps {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will come to meet me. Whatever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shows me, I will tell you." And he went off to a bare hill.
en.R: Then Balaam said to Balak, "Stay here next to your burnt offering. I will go away for a while. Maybe {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will come and meet me. I will tell you whatever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shows me." Then Balaam went to a bare hilltop.

es.L: Y dijo Balaam a Balac: «Ponte junto a tu holocausto, y déjame ir. Quizá {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} venga a mi encuentro, y la palabra que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me muestre, te la contaré». Y se fue a una altura pelada.
es.B: Entonces Balaam dijo a Balac: «Quédate aquí junto a tu holocausto mientras yo voy. Quizá {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} venga a encontrarse conmigo. Lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me muestre, te lo diré». Y se fue a un cerro pelado.
es.R: Entonces Balaam le dijo a Balac: «Quédate aquí al lado de tu holocausto. Yo me iré un rato. Tal vez {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} venga a mi encuentro. Te diré todo lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me muestre». Luego Balaam se fue a la cima de un cerro sin árboles.

fr.L: Et Balaam dit à Balak : « Tiens-toi près de ton holocauste, et je m’en irai. Peut-être {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} viendra-t-il à ma rencontre, et la parole qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me fera voir, je te la rapporterai. » Et il s’en alla sur une hauteur dénudée.
fr.B: Puis Balaam dit à Balak : « Reste ici près de ton holocauste pendant que je m’éloigne. Peut-être que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} viendra à ma rencontre. Ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me montrera, je te le dirai. » Et il partit vers une colline dénudée.
fr.R: Puis Balaam a dit à Balak : « Reste ici, à côté de ton holocauste. Moi, je vais m’éloigner un moment. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} viendra peut-être me rencontrer. Je te dirai tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me montrera. » Puis Balaam est parti vers le sommet d’une colline sans arbres.

sw.L: Kisha Balaamu akamwambia Balaki, "Simama kando ya sadaka yako ya kuteketezwa, nami nitakwenda. Huenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakuja kukutana nami, na neno lolote atakalonionyesha nitakuambia." Akaenda mpaka kilele kilicho wazi.
sw.B: Kisha Balaamu akamwambia Balaki, "Kaa hapa kando ya sadaka yako ya kuteketezwa, nami niende. Huenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakuja kukutana nami. Lolote atakalonionyesha, nitakuambia." Naye akaenda juu ya kilima kisicho na miti.
sw.R: Kisha Balaamu akamwambia Balaki, "Kaa hapa karibu na sadaka yako ya kuteketezwa. Mimi nitaondoka kwa muda. Labda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakuja kukutana nami. Nitakuambia lolote atakalonionyesha." Kisha Balaamu akaenda juu ya kilima kisicho na miti.

decisions.choice: perhaps the LORD will come to meet me: a meeting Balaam hopes for and cannot command
decisions.reason: The verb means to meet or to come upon, as by chance or by appointment; the same word is used in verses 4, 15 and 16. "Perhaps" shows that Balaam cannot make God appear or speak. In the story God comes to him each time (verses 4, 16).

decisions.choice: the word of whatever he shows me: whatever God makes known, by word or by sight
decisions.reason: "Shows" means to let someone see. What God reveals to a seer may be words or a vision (24:4, 16 speak of Balaam seeing "the vision of the Almighty"). Balaam promises to report it, whatever it is.

decisions.choice: a bare height: a treeless hill
decisions.reason: The word is rare. Elsewhere, in the plural, it means bare hills, open heights where nothing grows (Isaiah 41:18; Jeremiah 3:2; 4:11). Here it may be a high place from which to watch for a sign. A few readers take the word in the sense "alone" or "quietly": he went off by himself.

decisions.choice: Stay here beside your burnt offering
decisions.reason: The verb means to take one's stand. Balak is to stand by his offering, as the one who gave it, while Balaam goes to look for God's answer.

source.text: וַיִּקָּ֥ר אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־בִּלְעָ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו אֶת־שִׁבְעַ֤ת הַֽמִּזְבְּחֹת֙ עָרַ֔כְתִּי וָאַ֛עַל פָּ֥ר וָאַ֖יִל בַּמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And met God Balaam, and he said to him, the seven altars I have arranged, and I have offered up a bull and a ram on the altar.

en.L: And God met Balaam, and he said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "I have arranged the seven altars, and I have offered up a bull and a ram on [each] altar."
en.B: God met Balaam, and Balaam said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "I have set up the seven altars, and on each altar I have offered a bull and a ram."
en.R: God met Balaam there. Balaam said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "I have set up seven altars. I have offered a bull and a ram on each one."

es.L: Y Dios salió al encuentro de Balaam, y él {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «He dispuesto los siete altares, y he ofrecido un novillo y un carnero sobre [cada] altar».
es.B: Dios se encontró con Balaam, y Balaam {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «He preparado los siete altares, y en cada altar he ofrecido un novillo y un carnero».
es.R: Allí Dios se encontró con Balaam. Balaam {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «He levantado siete altares. En cada uno he ofrecido un novillo y un carnero».

fr.L: Et Dieu rencontra Balaam, et il {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « J’ai disposé les sept autels, et j’ai offert un taureau et un bélier sur [chaque] autel. »
fr.B: Dieu vint à la rencontre de Balaam, et Balaam {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « J’ai dressé les sept autels, et sur chaque autel j’ai offert un taureau et un bélier. »
fr.R: Dieu a rencontré Balaam à cet endroit. Balaam {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a dit : « J’ai installé sept autels. Sur chacun, j’ai offert un taureau et un bélier. »

sw.L: Naye Mungu akakutana na Balaamu, naye akamwambia, "Nimeziandaa madhabahu saba, nami nimetoa fahali mmoja na kondoo dume mmoja juu ya [kila] madhabahu."
sw.B: Mungu alikutana na Balaamu, na Balaamu akamwambia, "Nimezisimamisha madhabahu saba, na juu ya kila madhabahu nimetoa fahali na kondoo dume."
sw.R: Mungu alikutana na Balaamu huko. Balaamu akamwambia, "Nimejenga madhabahu saba. Juu ya kila moja nimetoa fahali mmoja na kondoo dume mmoja."

decisions.choice: he said to him: Balaam speaks to God
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he said to him". What is said, a report of the altars and offerings, shows that Balaam is the speaker and God the hearer.

decisions.choice: I have arranged the seven altars: Balaam presents the offerings as his own
decisions.reason: The verb means to lay out in order, as wood or offerings on an altar (Genesis 22:9; Leviticus 1:7-8). Balak had built the altars and both men had offered (verse 2), but Balaam speaks of them as his, as if the offering should earn a good word. God's answer in verse 5 does not mention them.

decisions.choice: Balaam said to him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker (m1).

source.text: וַיָּ֧שֶׂם יְהוָ֛ה דָּבָ֖ר בְּפִ֣י בִלְעָ֑ם וַיֹּ֛אמֶר שׁ֥וּב אֶל־בָּלָ֖ק וְכֹ֥ה תְדַבֵּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And put Yahweh a word in [the] mouth of Balaam, and he said, return to Balak, and thus you will speak.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} put a word in Balaam's mouth and said, "Return to Balak, and thus you shall speak."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} put a message in Balaam's mouth and said, "Go back to Balak and say this."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave Balaam a message to speak. He said, "Go back to Balak and tell him this message."

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} puso una palabra en la boca de Balaam, y dijo: «Vuelve a Balac, y así hablarás».
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} puso un mensaje en boca de Balaam y le dijo: «Regresa adonde está Balac y dile esto».
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio a Balaam un mensaje para que lo comunicara. Le dijo: «Vuelve con Balac y dale este mensaje».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} mit une parole dans la bouche de Balaam, et dit : « Retourne vers Balak, et c’est ainsi que tu parleras. »
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} mit un message dans la bouche de Balaam et lui dit : « Retourne auprès de Balak, et parle ainsi. »
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné à Balaam un message à transmettre. Il lui a dit : « Retourne voir Balak et transmets-lui ce message. »

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akatia neno kinywani mwa Balaamu, akasema, "Rudi kwa Balaki, na hivi ndivyo utakavyosema."
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliweka ujumbe kinywani mwa Balaamu, akasema, "Rudi kwa Balaki ukaseme hivi."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimpa Balaamu ujumbe wa kusema. Akamwambia, "Rudi kwa Balaki, umpe ujumbe huu."

decisions.choice: put a word in his mouth: give someone the very words to speak
decisions.reason: To put words in someone's mouth is to give them exactly what to say, as God promises to do for the prophet like Moses (Deuteronomy 18:18) and does for Jeremiah (Jeremiah 1:9). Balaam has already said he can speak only the word God puts in his mouth (22:38); he says it again in verse 12.

decisions.choice: thus you shall speak: refers to the words just given
decisions.reason: "Thus" points to the message God has put in Balaam's mouth, which he speaks in verses 7-10.

decisions.choice: gave Balaam a message to speak
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of putting a word in someone's mouth (m1).

source.text: וַיָּ֣שָׁב אֵלָ֔יו וְהִנֵּ֥ה נִצָּ֖ב עַל־עֹלָת֑וֹ ה֖וּא וְכָל־שָׂרֵ֥י מוֹאָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And he returned to him, and there! [he was] standing beside his burnt offering, he and all [the] officials of Moab.

en.L: And he returned to him, and there he was, standing beside his burnt offering, he and all the officials of Moab.
en.B: So he went back to Balak and found him standing beside his burnt offering with all the officials of Moab.
en.R: So Balaam went back to Balak. Balak was still standing beside his burnt offering, and all the leaders of Moab were with him.

es.L: Y volvió a él, y he aquí que estaba de pie junto a su holocausto, él y todos los príncipes de Moab.
es.B: Así que volvió adonde estaba Balac, y lo encontró de pie junto a su holocausto con todos los dignatarios de Moab.
es.R: Entonces Balaam volvió con Balac. Balac seguía de pie junto a su holocausto, y todos los jefes de Moab estaban con él.

fr.L: Et il revint vers lui, et voici qu’il se tenait près de son holocauste, lui et tous les princes de Moab.
fr.B: Il retourna donc auprès de Balak et le trouva debout près de son holocauste avec tous les dignitaires de Moab.
fr.R: Balaam est donc retourné auprès de Balak. Balak était toujours debout à côté de son holocauste, et tous les chefs de Moab étaient avec lui.

sw.L: Akarudi kwake, na tazama, alikuwa amesimama kando ya sadaka yake ya kuteketezwa, yeye na wakuu wote wa Moabu.
sw.B: Basi akarudi kwa Balaki, akamkuta amesimama kando ya sadaka yake ya kuteketezwa pamoja na maafisa wote wa Moabu.
sw.R: Basi Balaamu alirudi kwa Balaki. Balaki alikuwa bado amesimama karibu na sadaka yake ya kuteketezwa, na viongozi wote wa Moabu walikuwa pamoja naye.

decisions.choice: there he was, standing: what Balaam found on his return
decisions.reason: The word often rendered "behold" turns the reader's eyes to what Balaam saw: Balak waiting where Balaam had told him to stand (verse 3).

decisions.choice: officials of Moab: the king's leading men
decisions.reason: The word means a prince, chief or officer. These are the men Balak had sent to bring Balaam (22:8, 13-15, 21), now gathered to hear the curse.

decisions.choice: went back to Balak
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Balak, and Readable also names Balaam, where the Hebrew has "he" and "him".

source.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֥א מְשָׁל֖וֹ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר מִן־אֲ֠רָם יַנְחֵ֨נִי בָלָ֤ק מֶֽלֶךְ־מוֹאָב֙ מֵֽהַרְרֵי־קֶ֔דֶם לְכָה֙ אָֽרָה־לִּ֣י יַעֲקֹ֔ב וּלְכָ֖ה זֹעֲמָ֥ה יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And he lifted up his oracle and said, from Aram led me Balak, king of Moab, from [the] mountains of [the] east: come, curse for me Jacob, and come, denounce Israel.

en.L: And he took up his oracle and said, \q "From Aram Balak has led me, the king of Moab, from the mountains of the east: \q 'Come, curse Jacob for me, \q and come, denounce Israel.'
en.B: Then Balaam spoke his oracle: \q "Balak, king of Moab, brought me from Aram, from the mountains of the east: \q 'Come, curse Jacob for me; \q come, condemn Israel.'
en.R: Then Balaam gave his message: \q "Balak, the king of Moab, brought me from Aram, from the mountains in the east. \q He said, 'Come and curse the people of Jacob for me. \q Come and condemn Israel.'

es.L: Y profirió su oráculo y dijo: \q «Desde Aram me ha traído Balac, el rey de Moab, desde los montes del oriente: \q “Ven, maldíceme a Jacob, \q y ven, execra a Israel”.
es.B: Entonces Balaam pronunció su oráculo: \q «Balac, rey de Moab, me trajo desde Aram, desde los montes del oriente: \q “Ven, maldice a Jacob por mí; \q ven, condena a Israel”.
es.R: Entonces Balaam dio su mensaje: \q «Balac, el rey de Moab, me trajo desde Aram, desde los montes del este. \q Me dijo: “Ven a maldecir por mí al pueblo de Jacob. \q Ven a condenar a Israel”.

fr.L: Et il proféra son oracle et dit : \q « D’Aram Balak m’a fait venir, le roi de Moab, des montagnes de l’Orient : \q “Viens, maudis-moi Jacob, \q et viens, exècre Israël.”
fr.B: Alors Balaam prononça son oracle : \q « Balak, roi de Moab, m’a fait venir d’Aram, des montagnes de l’Orient : \q “Viens, maudis Jacob pour moi ; \q viens, condamne Israël !”
fr.R: Alors Balaam a transmis son message : \q « Balak, le roi de Moab, m’a fait venir d’Aram, des montagnes de l’est. \q Il m’a dit : “Viens maudire pour moi le peuple de Jacob. \q Viens condamner Israël.”

sw.L: Akatamka kauli yake, akasema, \q "Kutoka Aramu Balaki amenileta, mfalme wa Moabu, kutoka milima ya mashariki: \q 'Njoo, unilaanie Yakobo, \q na njoo, umshutumu Israeli.'
sw.B: Kisha Balaamu akatamka kauli yake ya kinabii: \q "Balaki, mfalme wa Moabu, amenileta kutoka Aramu, kutoka milima ya mashariki: \q 'Njoo, unilaanie Yakobo; \q njoo, umhukumu Israeli.'
sw.R: Kisha Balaamu akatoa ujumbe wake: \q "Balaki, mfalme wa Moabu, amenileta kutoka Aramu, kutoka milima ya mashariki. \q Alisema, 'Njoo uwalaani watu wa Yakobo kwa ajili yangu. \q Njoo uwahukumu Israeli.'

decisions.choice: took up his oracle: spoke a solemn saying in poetry
decisions.reason: The noun usually means a proverb or a saying built on comparison (1 Samuel 10:12; Proverbs 1:1), and sometimes a taunt song (Isaiah 14:4). Here it names Balaam's poetic oracles (also verse 18; 24:3, 15, 20, 21, 23). To "lift up" a saying is to raise the voice and speak it out.

decisions.choice: Aram, the mountains of the east: Balaam's homeland far to the northeast
decisions.reason: Balaam came from Pethor on the Euphrates (22:5), in Aram of the two rivers (Deuteronomy 23:5). "The east" names the lands beyond the desert east of Canaan, as in Genesis 29:1, where Jacob travels to the same region.

decisions.choice: curse ... denounce: call down harm and speak doom against
decisions.reason: The first verb is the usual word for a curse that calls harm on someone. The second means to speak in anger against someone, to condemn and doom them. Jacob and Israel are two names for the one people, descended from Jacob, whom God named Israel (Genesis 32:29); the poems pair them throughout.

decisions.choice: condemn
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "condemn" for the second verb, which Literal renders "denounce", and keep it in verse 8.

decisions.choice: He said ... the people of Jacob
decisions.reason: Readable says that Balak is the one speaking the quoted words and makes clear that Jacob means the people descended from him.

decisions.choice: "execra"
decisions.reason: Spanish "denunciar" now means to report someone. "Execrar" means to condemn and curse with authority, which is the sense of the second verb; Balanced and Readable say "condenar".

decisions.choice: "proféra son oracle" (L), "prononça son oracle" (B)
decisions.reason: French cannot "lift up" a saying; "proférer" keeps the solemn, spoken-aloud sense of the Hebrew verb, and "oracle" names Balaam's poems throughout chapters 23-24.

decisions.choice: "exècre"
decisions.reason: French "dénoncer" now means to report someone to the authorities. "Exécrer", in its older sense "to curse with solemn words", fits the second verb; Balanced and Readable say "condamner", as the English says "condemn".

decisions.choice: "akatamka kauli yake" (L), "kauli yake ya kinabii" (B); "akatoa ujumbe wake" (R)
decisions.reason: "Mithali" is a proverb, which would mislead here; "kauli" (a solemn statement) with "ya kinabii" names Balaam's oracles in all of chapters 23-24.

source.text: מָ֣ה אֶקֹּ֔ב לֹ֥א קַבֹּ֖ה אֵ֑ל וּמָ֣ה אֶזְעֹ֔ם לֹ֥א זָעַ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: How shall I curse [whom] not has cursed him God, and how shall I denounce [whom] not has denounced Yahweh?

en.L: How shall I curse [one whom] God has not cursed? \q And how shall I denounce [one whom] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has not denounced?
en.B: How can I curse a people God has not cursed? \q How can I condemn a people {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has not condemned?
en.R: God has not cursed them, so how can I curse them? \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has not condemned them, so how can I condemn them?

es.L: ¿Cómo maldeciré [a quien] Dios no ha maldecido? \q ¿Y cómo execraré [a quien] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no ha execrado?
es.B: ¿Cómo puedo maldecir a un pueblo que Dios no ha maldecido? \q ¿Cómo puedo condenar a un pueblo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no ha condenado?
es.R: Dios no los ha maldecido; ¿cómo podría yo maldecirlos? \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no los ha condenado; ¿cómo podría yo condenarlos?

fr.L: Comment maudirais-je [celui que] Dieu n’a pas maudit ? \q Et comment exécrerais-je [celui que] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} n’a pas exécré ?
fr.B: Comment pourrais-je maudire un peuple que Dieu n’a pas maudit ? \q Comment pourrais-je condamner un peuple que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} n’a pas condamné ?
fr.R: Dieu ne les a pas maudits : comment pourrais-je les maudire ? \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne les a pas condamnés : comment pourrais-je les condamner ?

sw.L: Nitamlaanije [yule ambaye] Mungu hakumlaani? \q Na nitamshutumuje [yule ambaye] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hakumshutumu?
sw.B: Ninawezaje kuwalaani watu ambao Mungu hakuwalaani? \q Ninawezaje kuwahukumu watu ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hakuwahukumu?
sw.R: Mungu hajawalaani; mimi nitawezaje kuwalaani? \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hajawahukumu; mimi nitawezaje kuwahukumu?

decisions.choice: how shall I curse ...?: a question that means "I cannot"
decisions.reason: The questions expect no answer. Balaam's words have power only as God gives them (22:18, 38), so a curse God has not spoken cannot be spoken by Balaam.

decisions.choice: curse: a second word for cursing, used by Balak
decisions.reason: This verb is a different word from the one in verse 7, but with the same sense. It is the word Balak uses in his demands (22:11, 17; 23:11, 13, 27), and Balaam answers with it.

decisions.choice: God ... the LORD: the same God named two ways
decisions.reason: The two lines name God first with the general word for God and then with his own name, the LORD, the God of Israel. The poem treats them as one: the God of Israel is the only one whose word counts here.

decisions.choice: a people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "him", meaning Israel as one people. Balanced says "a people"; Literal brackets "[one whom]".

decisions.choice: "maldecir"
decisions.reason: In Balak's prose demands this verb is "echar una maldición" (chapter 22); in the poem the plain verb keeps the lines balanced, with the same sense.

decisions.choice: "maudire"
decisions.reason: In Balak's prose demands this verb is "lancer une malédiction contre" (chapter 22); in the poem the short "maudire" keeps the two lines balanced, and the sense is the same (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "kulaani"
decisions.reason: Chapter 22 renders this verb "kuapiza" in prose; in the poem "kulaani" keeps the two lines parallel and is the plainer word for the same act.

source.text: כִּֽי־מֵרֹ֤אשׁ צֻרִים֙ אֶרְאֶ֔נּוּ וּמִגְּבָע֖וֹת אֲשׁוּרֶ֑נּוּ הֶן־עָם֙ לְבָדָ֣ד יִשְׁכֹּ֔ן וּבַגּוֹיִ֖ם לֹ֥א יִתְחַשָּֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: For from [the] top of rocks I see him, and from hills I watch him; there! a people alone it dwells, and among the nations not it reckons itself.

en.L: For from the top of [the] rocks I see him, \q and from [the] hills I watch him; \q look, a people dwelling alone, \q and it does not count itself among the nations.
en.B: From the tops of the rocks I see them; \q from the hills I watch them. \q Here is a people that lives apart \q and does not count itself as one of the nations.
en.R: From the tops of the rocks I can see them. \q From the hills I watch them. \q They are a people who live apart. \q They do not think of themselves as one of the other nations.

es.L: Porque desde la cumbre de [las] rocas lo veo, \q y desde [las] colinas lo observo; \q he aquí un pueblo que habita solo, \q y no se cuenta entre las naciones.
es.B: Desde lo alto de las rocas los veo; \q desde las colinas los contemplo. \q Es un pueblo que vive aparte \q y no se tiene por una de tantas naciones.
es.R: Desde lo alto de las rocas puedo verlos. \q Desde las colinas los observo. \q Son un pueblo que vive apartado. \q No se ven a sí mismos como una nación más.

fr.L: Car du sommet des rochers je le vois, \q et des collines je l’observe ; \q voici, un peuple qui demeure à l’écart, \q et il ne se compte pas parmi les nations.
fr.B: Du haut des rochers je les vois ; \q des collines je les contemple. \q Voici un peuple qui vit à part \q et ne se range pas parmi les nations.
fr.R: Du haut des rochers, je peux les voir. \q Depuis les collines, je les regarde. \q C’est un peuple qui vit à part. \q Ils ne se considèrent pas comme une nation parmi les autres.

sw.L: Kwa maana kutoka kilele cha miamba namwona, \q na kutoka vilimani namtazama; \q tazama, watu wakaao peke yao, \q wala hawajihesabu miongoni mwa mataifa.
sw.B: Kutoka vilele vya miamba nawaona; \q kutoka vilimani nawatazama. \q Hawa ni watu wanaoishi peke yao, \q wala hawajihesabu kuwa mmoja wa mataifa.
sw.R: Kutoka juu ya miamba naweza kuwaona. \q Kutoka vilimani nawatazama. \q Ni watu wanaoishi kando, peke yao. \q Hawajioni kuwa taifa kama mataifa mengine.

decisions.choice: I see him: Israel spoken of as one person
decisions.reason: "Him" is the people Israel, called Jacob in verse 7, spoken of as one man. Balaam is looking down on the camp from the heights where Balak has brought him (22:41).

decisions.choice: a people dwelling alone: set apart, and secure
decisions.reason: To dwell alone is to live apart from others and undisturbed. Israel is a people set apart by God (Exodus 33:16; Leviticus 20:26), and "alone" also carries the sense of safety, as in Deuteronomy 33:28, "Israel dwells in safety, alone".

decisions.choice: does not count itself among the nations
decisions.reason: The verb is reflexive: Israel does not reckon itself one of the nations. It could also be read "is not counted among the nations" by others; either way Israel stands apart.

decisions.choice: them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "them" for the people that the Hebrew calls "him" (m1). Literal keeps "him".

decisions.choice: From the tops of the rocks ... (no "for")
decisions.reason: The opening "for" links what Balaam sees to his refusal in verse 8. Balanced and Readable start the new line without it, since the link is clear from the order of the lines.

source.text: מִ֤י מָנָה֙ עֲפַ֣ר יַעֲקֹ֔ב וּמִסְפָּ֖ר אֶת־רֹ֣בַע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל תָּמֹ֤ת נַפְשִׁי֙ מ֣וֹת יְשָׁרִ֔ים וּתְהִ֥י אַחֲרִיתִ֖י כָּמֹֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Who has counted [the] dust of Jacob, and [by] number the fourth part of Israel? Let die my soul [the] death of [the] upright, and let be my end like his.

en.L: Who has counted the dust of Jacob, \q or numbered the fourth part of Israel? \q Let my soul die the death of the upright, \q and let my end be like his!"
en.B: Who can count the dust of Jacob \q or number even a fourth of Israel? \q Let me die the death of the upright, \q and may my end be like theirs!"
en.R: Jacob's people are as many as the specks of dust. Who could count them? \q Who could count even a fourth of Israel? \q I want to die like these people who do what is right. \q I want my end to be like theirs!"

es.L: ¿Quién ha contado el polvo de Jacob, \q o numerado la cuarta parte de Israel? \q ¡Muera mi alma la muerte de los rectos, \q y sea mi final como el suyo!».
es.B: ¿Quién puede contar el polvo de Jacob \q o calcular siquiera la cuarta parte de Israel? \q ¡Que muera yo como mueren los rectos, \q y que mi final sea como el de ellos!».
es.R: El pueblo de Jacob es tan numeroso como las partículas de polvo. ¿Quién podría contarlos? \q ¿Quién podría contar siquiera la cuarta parte de Israel? \q Quiero morir como esta gente que hace lo recto. \q ¡Quiero que mi final sea como el de ellos!».

fr.L: Qui a compté la poussière de Jacob, \q ou dénombré le quart d’Israël ? \q Que mon âme meure de la mort de ceux qui sont droits, \q et que ma fin soit comme la sienne ! »
fr.B: Qui peut compter la poussière de Jacob \q ou dénombrer ne serait-ce que le quart d’Israël ? \q Que je meure comme meurent ceux qui sont droits, \q et que ma fin ressemble à la leur ! »
fr.R: Le peuple de Jacob est aussi nombreux que les grains de poussière. Qui pourrait les compter ? \q Qui pourrait compter ne serait-ce qu’un quart d’Israël ? \q Je voudrais mourir comme ces gens qui font ce qui est juste. \q Je voudrais que ma fin soit comme la leur ! »

sw.L: Ni nani aliyeyahesabu mavumbi ya Yakobo, \q au kuihesabu robo ya Israeli? \q Nafsi yangu na ife kifo cha wanyoofu, \q na mwisho wangu na uwe kama wake!"
sw.B: Ni nani awezaye kuyahesabu mavumbi ya Yakobo, \q au kuhesabu hata robo ya Israeli? \q Na nife kifo cha wanyoofu, \q na mwisho wangu uwe kama mwisho wao!"
sw.R: Watu wa Yakobo ni wengi kama chembe za mavumbi. Ni nani awezaye kuwahesabu? \q Ni nani awezaye kuhesabu hata robo ya Israeli? \q Ningependa kufa kama watu hawa wanaotenda yaliyo sawa. \q Ningependa mwisho wangu uwe kama mwisho wao!"

decisions.choice: the dust of Jacob: descendants as many as the dust
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham and Jacob offspring "like the dust of the earth" (Genesis 13:16; 28:14). Balaam sees the promise kept: the question "who has counted" means that no one can.

decisions.choice: the fourth part of Israel: even a quarter of the people is past counting
decisions.reason: The word means a fourth part. It may refer to one of the four groups of tribes camped around the tabernacle (chapter 2), the part Balaam can see (verse 13). Some take it instead as a word for a cloud of dust, matching "dust" in the line before. The ancient Greek translation reads "the clans of Israel".

decisions.choice: let my soul die: let me die
decisions.reason: "My soul" here means "I myself", the whole living person, as often in Hebrew poetry.

decisions.choice: the death of the upright ... my end like his: a peaceful death and a lasting future, like Israel's
decisions.reason: "The upright" are Israel, the people who belong to God. "End" can mean the close of life or what comes after it, one's future and descendants. "His" refers back to Israel as one people. Balaam wishes for himself what he sees God giving Israel; later he dies by the sword among Israel's enemies (31:8).

decisions.choice: like theirs
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "theirs" for the singular "his", which refers to Israel as one people, matching "them" in verse 9.

decisions.choice: Jacob's people are as many as the specks of dust. Who could count them?
decisions.reason: Readable states the comparison first and then asks the question, so that the picture of the dust is clear (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בָּלָק֙ אֶל־בִּלְעָ֔ם מֶ֥ה עָשִׂ֖יתָ לִ֑י לָקֹ֤ב אֹיְבַי֙ לְקַחְתִּ֔יךָ וְהִנֵּ֖ה בֵּרַ֥כְתָּ בָרֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Balak to Balaam, what have you done to me? To curse my enemies I took you, and there! you have blessed, blessing.

en.L: And Balak said to Balaam, "What have you done to me? I took you to curse my enemies, and look, you have done nothing but bless [them]!"
en.B: Balak said to Balaam, "What have you done to me? I brought you here to curse my enemies, and instead you have done nothing but bless them!"
en.R: Balak said to Balaam, "What have you done to me? I brought you here to curse my enemies. But all you have done is bless them!"

es.L: Y dijo Balac a Balaam: «¿Qué me has hecho? Te tomé para echar una maldición a mis enemigos, y he aquí que [los] has bendecido de lleno».
es.B: Balac dijo a Balaam: «¿Qué me has hecho? Te traje para echar una maldición a mis enemigos, y en lugar de eso no has hecho más que bendecirlos».
es.R: Balac le dijo a Balaam: «¿Qué me has hecho? Te traje aquí para maldecir a mis enemigos. ¡Pero lo único que has hecho es bendecirlos!».

fr.L: Et Balak dit à Balaam : « Que m’as-tu fait ? Je t’ai pris pour lancer une malédiction contre mes ennemis, et voici, tu n’as fait que [les] bénir ! »
fr.B: Balak dit à Balaam : « Que m’as-tu fait ? Je t’ai fait venir pour lancer une malédiction contre mes ennemis, et au contraire tu n’as fait que les bénir ! »
fr.R: Balak a dit à Balaam : « Qu’est-ce que tu m’as fait ? Je t’ai fait venir pour maudire mes ennemis. Et toi, tu n’as fait que les bénir ! »

sw.L: Naye Balaki akamwambia Balaamu, "Umenifanyia nini? Nilikuchukua uwaapize adui zangu, na tazama, umewabariki kabisa!"
sw.B: Balaki alimwambia Balaamu, "Umenitendea nini? Nilikuleta hapa uwaapize adui zangu, lakini badala yake umewabariki tu!"
sw.R: Balaki alimwambia Balaamu, "Umenifanyia nini? Nilikuleta hapa ili uwalaani adui zangu. Lakini wewe umewabariki tu!"

decisions.choice: you have blessed, blessing: you have blessed them outright
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. Balak complains that Balaam has not merely failed to curse; he has given Israel a full blessing.

decisions.choice: I took you: I had you brought here
decisions.reason: Balak had sent messengers twice to fetch Balaam (22:5-6, 15-17). "Took" means he brought Balaam at his cost and for his purpose.

decisions.choice: bless [them] / bless them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives no object for "blessed"; it is plainly the enemies just named. Literal brackets the word.

source.text: וַיַּ֖עַן וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הֲלֹ֗א אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָשִׂ֤ים יְהוָה֙ בְּפִ֔י אֹת֥וֹ אֶשְׁמֹ֖ר לְדַבֵּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he answered and said, [is it] not what puts Yahweh in my mouth, it I must take care to speak?

en.L: And he answered and said, "Is it not what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} puts in my mouth that I must take care to speak?"
en.B: Balaam answered, "Do I not have to be careful to say what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} puts in my mouth?"
en.R: Balaam answered, "I must say exactly what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives me to say."

es.L: Y respondió y dijo: «¿No es lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} pone en mi boca lo que debo cuidar de decir?».
es.B: Balaam respondió: «¿Acaso no debo tener cuidado de decir lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} pone en mi boca?».
es.R: Balaam respondió: «Tengo que decir exactamente lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me da para decir».

fr.L: Et il répondit et dit : « N’est-ce pas ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} met dans ma bouche que je dois prendre soin de dire ? »
fr.B: Balaam répondit : « Ne dois-je pas veiller à dire ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} met dans ma bouche ? »
fr.R: Balaam a répondu : « Je dois dire exactement ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me donne à dire. »

sw.L: Naye akajibu, akasema, "Je, si lile ambalo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analitia kinywani mwangu ndilo ninalopaswa kujihadhari kulisema?"
sw.B: Balaamu akajibu, "Je, sipaswi kuwa mwangalifu kusema kile ambacho {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anakitia kinywani mwangu?"
sw.R: Balaamu akajibu, "Ni lazima niseme sawasawa kile ambacho {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ananipa kusema."

decisions.choice: is it not ...?: a question that means "of course"
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer yes. Balaam answers Balak's complaint by repeating what he said when he arrived (22:38).

decisions.choice: take care: keep, watch over
decisions.reason: The verb means to keep or guard. Balaam must keep watch over his words, so that he says what God gives him and nothing else.

decisions.choice: I must say exactly what the LORD gives me to say.
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies (m1), and explains "puts in my mouth" as in verse 5.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו בָּלָ֗ק לְכָה־נָּ֨א אִתִּ֜י אֶל־מָק֤וֹם אַחֵר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּרְאֶ֣נּוּ מִשָּׁ֔ם אֶ֚פֶס קָצֵ֣הוּ תִרְאֶ֔ה וְכֻלּ֖וֹ לֹ֣א תִרְאֶ֑ה וְקָבְנוֹ־לִ֖י מִשָּֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him Balak, come, please, with me to another place where you will see it from there; only its edge you will see, and all of it you will not see; and curse it for me from there.

en.L: And Balak said to him, "Come with me, please, to another place from which you will see it. You will see only the edge of it, and you will not see all of it. Then curse it for me from there."
en.B: Then Balak said to him, "Please come with me to another place where you can see them. You will see only the outer edge of them, not all of them. Curse them for me from there."
en.R: Then Balak said to him, "Please come with me to another place. From there you will be able to see the people of Israel, but only the edge of their camp, not all of them. Curse them for me from there."

es.L: Y le dijo Balac: «Ven, te ruego, conmigo a otro lugar desde donde lo verás. Solo verás su extremo, y no lo verás todo. Y échale una maldición por mí desde allí».
es.B: Entonces Balac le dijo: «Por favor, ven conmigo a otro lugar desde donde puedas verlos. Solo verás a los del extremo, no a todos. Échales una maldición por mí desde allí».
es.R: Entonces Balac le dijo: «Por favor, ven conmigo a otro lugar. Desde allí podrás ver al pueblo de Israel, pero solo el borde de su campamento, no a todos. Maldícelos por mí desde allí».

fr.L: Et Balak lui dit : « Viens donc avec moi dans un autre lieu d’où tu le verras. Tu n’en verras que l’extrémité, et tu ne le verras pas tout entier. Et de là, lance pour moi une malédiction contre lui. »
fr.B: Balak lui dit alors : « Viens, je te prie, avec moi dans un autre endroit d’où tu pourras les voir. Tu n’en verras que la bordure, pas le peuple entier. De là, lance pour moi une malédiction contre eux. »
fr.R: Alors Balak lui a dit : « S’il te plaît, viens avec moi à un autre endroit. De là, tu pourras voir le peuple d’Israël, mais seulement le bord de leur camp, pas tout le monde. De là, maudis-les pour moi. »

sw.L: Naye Balaki akamwambia, "Tafadhali, njoo pamoja nami mahali pengine ambapo utamwona kutoka huko. Utaona ukingo wake tu, wala hutamwona wote; kisha umwapize kwa ajili yangu kutoka huko."
sw.B: Kisha Balaki akamwambia, "Tafadhali, njoo pamoja nami mahali pengine ambapo utaweza kuwaona. Utaona ukingo wao tu, si wote. Uwaapize kwa ajili yangu ukiwa huko."
sw.R: Kisha Balaki akamwambia, "Tafadhali, njoo pamoja nami mahali pengine. Kutoka huko utaweza kuwaona Waisraeli, lakini ukingo wa kambi yao tu, si wote. Uwalaani kwa ajili yangu ukiwa huko."

decisions.choice: you will see only the edge of it: the new place gives only a partial view
alternatives: (here) you see only the edge of them, not all of them
decisions.reason: The verbs can be read as future, describing the new place: from there Balaam will see only part of Israel, perhaps so that the sight of the whole people does not move him to bless again (verses 9-10). They can also be read as present, describing where they stand now: "here you see only the edge of it, not all of it", as in 22:41, where Balaam first saw "the edge of the people". Then Balak would be offering a fuller view.

decisions.choice: it: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "it" or "him", in the singular, for the people camped below, as in 22:41.

decisions.choice: them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "them" for the people (m2); Literal keeps "it".

decisions.choice: the people of Israel ... the edge of their camp
decisions.reason: Readable names the people and says that the edge is the edge of the camp, as the context makes plain.

source.text: וַיִּקָּחֵ֨הוּ֙ שְׂדֵ֣ה צֹפִ֔ים אֶל־רֹ֖אשׁ הַפִּסְגָּ֑ה וַיִּ֨בֶן֙ שִׁבְעָ֣ה מִזְבְּחֹ֔ת וַיַּ֛עַל פָּ֥ר וָאַ֖יִל בַּמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he took him [to the] field of Zophim, to [the] top of the Pisgah, and he built seven altars and offered up a bull and a ram on the altar.

en.L: And he took him to the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, and he built seven altars and offered up a bull and a ram on [each] altar.
en.B: So he took him to the field of Zophim on the top of Pisgah. There he built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
en.R: So Balak took Balaam to a field called Zophim, at the top of the Pisgah ridge. He built seven altars there and offered a bull and a ram on each one.

es.L: Y lo llevó al campo de Zofim, a la cumbre del Pisga, y edificó siete altares y ofreció un novillo y un carnero sobre [cada] altar.
es.B: Así que lo llevó al campo de Zofim, en la cumbre del Pisga. Allí edificó siete altares y ofreció un novillo y un carnero en cada altar.
es.R: Entonces Balac llevó a Balaam a un campo llamado Zofim, en lo alto de la sierra del Pisga. Allí construyó siete altares y ofreció un novillo y un carnero en cada uno.

fr.L: Et il le conduisit au champ de Tsophim, au sommet du Pisga, et il bâtit sept autels et offrit un taureau et un bélier sur [chaque] autel.
fr.B: Il l’emmena donc au champ de Tsophim, au sommet du Pisga. Là, il bâtit sept autels et offrit un taureau et un bélier sur chaque autel.
fr.R: Alors Balak a emmené Balaam dans un champ appelé Tsophim, au sommet de la chaîne du Pisga. Il a construit là sept autels et a offert un taureau et un bélier sur chacun.

sw.L: Akamchukua mpaka uwanda wa Sofimu, mpaka kilele cha Pisga, akajenga madhabahu saba, akatoa fahali mmoja na kondoo dume mmoja juu ya [kila] madhabahu.
sw.B: Basi akampeleka katika uwanda wa Sofimu juu ya kilele cha Pisga. Huko akajenga madhabahu saba, akatoa fahali na kondoo dume juu ya kila madhabahu.
sw.R: Basi Balaki alimpeleka Balaamu mahali paitwapo Sofimu, juu ya safu ya milima ya Pisga. Akajenga huko madhabahu saba, akatoa fahali mmoja na kondoo dume mmoja juu ya kila moja.

decisions.choice: the field of Zophim, the top of Pisgah: a lookout on the heights above the Jordan valley
decisions.reason: Zophim means "watchers" or "lookouts": the place was a lookout post. Pisgah is a ridge at the edge of the Moabite plateau, looking down over the plains where Israel was camped (21:20). From its top Moses would later see the promised land before he died (Deuteronomy 3:27; 34:1).

decisions.choice: on the altar: on each altar
decisions.reason: As in verse 2. Here Balak builds the altars and makes the offerings himself, following Balaam's instructions of verse 1.

decisions.choice: the Pisgah ridge
decisions.reason: Readable says what Pisgah was, a ridge of hills, as the Hebrew article ("the Pisgah") suggests.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־בָּלָ֔ק הִתְיַצֵּ֥ב כֹּ֖ה עַל־עֹלָתֶ֑ךָ וְאָנֹכִ֖י אִקָּ֥רֶה כֹּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to Balak, station yourself here beside your burnt offering, and I, I will meet [him] there.

en.L: And he said to Balak, "Station yourself here beside your burnt offering, while I meet [God] over there."
en.B: Balaam said to Balak, "Stay here beside your burnt offering while I go over there to meet with God."
en.R: Balaam said to Balak, "Stay here next to your burnt offering. I will go over there to meet with God."

es.L: Y dijo a Balac: «Ponte aquí junto a tu holocausto, mientras yo me encuentro [con Dios] allá».
es.B: Balaam dijo a Balac: «Quédate aquí junto a tu holocausto mientras yo voy allá a encontrarme con Dios».
es.R: Balaam le dijo a Balac: «Quédate aquí al lado de tu holocausto. Yo iré allá para encontrarme con Dios».

fr.L: Et il dit à Balak : « Tiens-toi ici près de ton holocauste, tandis que moi, je rencontrerai [Dieu] là-bas. »
fr.B: Balaam dit à Balak : « Reste ici près de ton holocauste pendant que je vais là-bas à la rencontre de Dieu. »
fr.R: Balaam a dit à Balak : « Reste ici, à côté de ton holocauste. Moi, je vais aller là-bas pour rencontrer Dieu. »

sw.L: Naye akamwambia Balaki, "Simama hapa kando ya sadaka yako ya kuteketezwa, nami nitakutana [na Mungu] kule."
sw.B: Balaamu akamwambia Balaki, "Kaa hapa kando ya sadaka yako ya kuteketezwa, nami niende kule nikakutane na Mungu."
sw.R: Balaamu akamwambia Balaki, "Kaa hapa karibu na sadaka yako ya kuteketezwa. Mimi nitakwenda kule kukutana na Mungu."

decisions.choice: here ... over there: the same small word used twice for two places
decisions.reason: The word usually means "thus" or "so", but it can also point to a place. Here it is used twice: Balak is to stand "here", and Balaam will go "there".

decisions.choice: I will meet: the one met is God
decisions.reason: The verb has no object; it is the same verb as in verses 3-4 ("come to meet me"). Verse 16 shows that it was the LORD who met him. The pronoun "I" is stressed: Balak waits while Balaam alone goes to meet God.

decisions.choice: meet [God] / meet with God
decisions.reason: All levels name the one Balaam goes to meet (m2); Literal brackets the word, and Balanced and Readable add "go".

source.text: וַיִּקָּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־בִּלְעָ֔ם וַיָּ֥שֶׂם דָּבָ֖ר בְּפִ֑יו וַיֹּ֛אמֶר שׁ֥וּב אֶל־בָּלָ֖ק וְכֹ֥ה תְדַבֵּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And met Yahweh Balaam, and he put a word in his mouth and said, return to Balak, and thus you will speak.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} met Balaam and put a word in his mouth and said, "Return to Balak, and thus you shall speak."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} met Balaam, put a message in his mouth, and said, "Go back to Balak and say this."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} met Balaam and gave him a message to speak. He said, "Go back to Balak and tell him this message."

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} salió al encuentro de Balaam y puso una palabra en su boca, y dijo: «Vuelve a Balac, y así hablarás».
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se encontró con Balaam, puso un mensaje en su boca y le dijo: «Regresa adonde está Balac y dile esto».
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se encontró con Balaam y le dio un mensaje para que lo comunicara. Le dijo: «Vuelve con Balac y dale este mensaje».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} rencontra Balaam, et mit une parole dans sa bouche, et dit : « Retourne vers Balak, et c’est ainsi que tu parleras. »
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vint à la rencontre de Balaam, mit un message dans sa bouche et lui dit : « Retourne auprès de Balak, et parle ainsi. »
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a rencontré Balaam et lui a donné un message à transmettre. Il lui a dit : « Retourne voir Balak et transmets-lui ce message. »

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akakutana na Balaamu, akatia neno kinywani mwake, akasema, "Rudi kwa Balaki, na hivi ndivyo utakavyosema."
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikutana na Balaamu, akaweka ujumbe kinywani mwake, akasema, "Rudi kwa Balaki ukaseme hivi."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikutana na Balaamu, akampa ujumbe wa kusema. Akamwambia, "Rudi kwa Balaki, umpe ujumbe huu."

decisions.choice: the LORD met Balaam: the same God as in verse 4
decisions.reason: As in verse 5. Verse 4 says "God" met Balaam; here the narrator uses the LORD's own name. The story uses both for the one God of Israel (22:9, 20, 22).

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֣א אֵלָ֗יו וְהִנּ֤וֹ נִצָּב֙ עַל־עֹ֣לָת֔וֹ וְשָׂרֵ֥י מוֹאָ֖ב אִתּ֑וֹ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ בָּלָ֔ק מַה־דִּבֶּ֖ר יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he came to him, and there! he [was] standing beside his burnt offering, and [the] officials of Moab with him. And said to him Balak, what has spoken Yahweh?

en.L: And he came to him, and there he was, standing beside his burnt offering, and the officials of Moab with him. And Balak said to him, "What has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoken?"
en.B: So he came to Balak and found him standing beside his burnt offering with the officials of Moab. Balak asked him, "What did {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} say?"
en.R: So Balaam came back to Balak. Balak was standing beside his burnt offering, and the leaders of Moab were with him. Balak asked, "What did {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} say?"

es.L: Y vino a él, y he aquí que estaba de pie junto a su holocausto, y los príncipes de Moab con él. Y le dijo Balac: «¿Qué ha hablado {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}?».
es.B: Así que fue adonde estaba Balac y lo encontró de pie junto a su holocausto con los dignatarios de Moab. Balac le preguntó: «¿Qué dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}?».
es.R: Entonces Balaam volvió con Balac. Balac estaba de pie junto a su holocausto, y los jefes de Moab estaban con él. Balac le preguntó: «¿Qué dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}?».

fr.L: Et il vint vers lui, et voici qu’il se tenait près de son holocauste, et les princes de Moab avec lui. Et Balak lui dit : « Qu’a dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ? »
fr.B: Il revint donc auprès de Balak et le trouva debout près de son holocauste avec les dignitaires de Moab. Balak lui demanda : « Qu’a dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ? »
fr.R: Balaam est donc revenu auprès de Balak. Balak était debout à côté de son holocauste, et les chefs de Moab étaient avec lui. Balak lui a demandé : « Qu’est-ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit ? »

sw.L: Akamjia, na tazama, alikuwa amesimama kando ya sadaka yake ya kuteketezwa, na wakuu wa Moabu pamoja naye. Naye Balaki akamwambia, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesema nini?"
sw.B: Basi akamjia Balaki, akamkuta amesimama kando ya sadaka yake ya kuteketezwa pamoja na maafisa wa Moabu. Balaki akamwuliza, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesema nini?"
sw.R: Basi Balaamu alirudi kwa Balaki. Balaki alikuwa amesimama karibu na sadaka yake ya kuteketezwa, na viongozi wa Moabu walikuwa pamoja naye. Balaki akamwuliza, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesema nini?"

decisions.choice: what has the LORD spoken?: Balak now asks for the word of Israel's God
decisions.reason: After the first oracle Balak knows that Balaam's words come from the LORD (22:8, 18; 23:12). His question names the LORD, the God of Israel, whose word he hopes will change.

decisions.choice: came to Balak
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, Balanced and Readable name the people the Hebrew calls "he" and "him".

source.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֥א מְשָׁל֖וֹ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר ק֤וּם בָּלָק֙ וּֽשֲׁמָ֔ע הַאֲזִ֥ינָה עָדַ֖י בְּנ֥וֹ צִפֹּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he lifted up his oracle and said, arise, Balak, and hear; give ear to me, son of Zippor.

en.L: And he took up his oracle and said, \q "Rise, Balak, and hear; \q give ear to me, son of Zippor.
en.B: Then Balaam spoke his oracle: \q "Rise, Balak, and listen; \q hear me, son of Zippor.
en.R: Then Balaam gave his message: \q "Pay attention, Balak, and listen. \q Hear what I say, son of Zippor.

es.L: Y profirió su oráculo y dijo: \q «Levántate, Balac, y oye; \q préstame oído, hijo de Zipor.
es.B: Entonces Balaam pronunció su oráculo: \q «Levántate, Balac, y escucha; \q óyeme, hijo de Zipor.
es.R: Entonces Balaam dio su mensaje: \q «Presta atención, Balac, y escucha. \q Oye lo que digo, hijo de Zipor.

fr.L: Et il proféra son oracle et dit : \q « Lève-toi, Balak, et entends ; \q prête-moi l’oreille, fils de Tsippor.
fr.B: Alors Balaam prononça son oracle : \q « Lève-toi, Balak, et écoute ; \q entends-moi, fils de Tsippor.
fr.R: Alors Balaam a transmis son message : \q « Fais bien attention, Balak, et écoute. \q Entends ce que je dis, fils de Tsippor.

sw.L: Akatamka kauli yake, akasema, \q "Inuka, Balaki, usikie; \q nitegee sikio, ewe mwana wa Sipori.
sw.B: Kisha Balaamu akatamka kauli yake ya kinabii: \q "Inuka, Balaki, usikilize; \q nisikie, ewe mwana wa Sipori.
sw.R: Kisha Balaamu akatoa ujumbe wake: \q "Sikiliza kwa makini, Balaki. \q Sikia ninachosema, ewe mwana wa Sipori.

decisions.choice: rise: a call to attention
decisions.reason: Balak is already standing (verse 17), so "rise" is not an order to stand up. It is a call to rouse oneself and pay attention, as at the start of a solemn speech (Judges 3:20 shows a king rising to hear a word from God).

decisions.choice: give ear: listen closely
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the word for "ear". It is the formal call to listen that opens many poems (Deuteronomy 32:1; Isaiah 1:2). "Son of Zippor" names Balak by his father, as in 22:2.

decisions.choice: Pay attention
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "rise" here (m1), since "stand up" would mislead.

source.text: לֹ֣א אִ֥ישׁ אֵל֙ וִֽיכַזֵּ֔ב וּבֶן־אָדָ֖ם וְיִתְנֶחָ֑ם הַה֤וּא אָמַר֙ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲשֶׂ֔ה וְדִבֶּ֖ר וְלֹ֥א יְקִימֶֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: Not [is] a man God, that he should lie, and a son of humankind, that he should change his mind. He, has he said, and not will he do? And has he spoken, and not will he make it stand?

en.L: God [is] not {{gender:a human|a man}}, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} should lie, \q nor a son of {{gender:humankind|man}}, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} should change {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind. \q Has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, and will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not do [it]? \q Or has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoken, and will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not make it stand?
en.B: God is not {{gender:a human|a man}}, who might lie, \q nor a mortal, who might change course. \q Would {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} say something and not do it? \q Would {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} speak and not make it happen?
en.R: God is not a human being who would lie. \q He does not take back what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has decided. \q When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says something, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does it. \q When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes a promise, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} keeps it.

es.L: Dios no [es] {{gender:un ser humano|un hombre}} para mentir, \q ni un hijo {{gender:de la humanidad|de hombre}} para cambiar de parecer. \q ¿Lo ha dicho {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y no [lo] hará? \q ¿O ha hablado, y no lo llevará a cabo?
es.B: Dios no es {{gender:un ser humano|un hombre}}, capaz de mentir, \q ni un mortal, que cambie de rumbo. \q ¿Diría {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} algo para luego no hacerlo? \q ¿Hablaría sin hacerlo realidad?
es.R: Dios no es un ser humano que diga mentiras. \q No se echa atrás de lo que ha decidido. \q Cuando dice algo, lo hace. \q Cuando promete algo, lo cumple.

fr.L: Dieu n’[est] pas {{gender:un être humain|un homme}}, pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} mente, \q ni un {{gender:fils de l’humanité|fils d’homme}}, pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se ravise. \q A-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit, et ne fera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pas ? \q Ou a-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} parlé, et ne le fera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pas tenir ?
fr.B: Dieu n’est pas {{gender:un être humain|un homme}}, qui pourrait mentir, \q ni un mortel, qui pourrait changer d’avis. \q Dirait-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} une chose sans la faire ? \q Parlerait-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sans l’accomplir ?
fr.R: Dieu n’est pas un être humain qui dirait des mensonges. \q Il ne revient pas sur ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a décidé. \q Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit quelque chose, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le fait. \q Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} promet, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} tient parole.

sw.L: Mungu si mwanadamu, hata aseme uongo, \q wala si mwana wa binadamu, hata abadili nia yake. \q Je, amesema jambo, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} hatalitenda? \q Au amenena, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} hatalisimamisha?
sw.B: Mungu si mwanadamu, ambaye angeweza kusema uongo, \q wala si mtu wa kufa, ambaye angebadili mwelekeo. \q Je, angesema jambo kisha asilitende? \q Je, angenena kisha asilitimize?
sw.R: Mungu si binadamu anayesema uongo. \q Habadilishi kile alichokwisha kuamua. \q Akisema jambo, hulitenda. \q Akiahidi, hutimiza ahadi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

decisions.choice: a man ... a son of humankind: a human being, a mortal
decisions.reason: The first word usually means a man; set against God, it means any human being. "Son of humankind" is a Hebrew way to say "a mortal". The contrast is between God and the weakness and changeableness of people.

decisions.choice: change his mind: go back on what he has decided
decisions.reason: The verb means to relent, to regret or to change one's mind. The same saying returns in 1 Samuel 15:29. Elsewhere God does relent from a threatened judgment when people turn (Exodus 32:14; Jeremiah 18:7-10). The point here is that God will not take back the blessing he has given Israel because a king pays a seer to curse them.

decisions.choice: has he said, and will he not do it?: questions that mean "he will"
decisions.reason: The questions expect the answer that God always does what he has said. "Make it stand" means to carry out or fulfill a word or promise.

decisions.choice: change course / take back what he has decided; make it happen / keeps it
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable choose wording that keeps "his" clearly about God (m2) and give the sense of "make it stand" (m3).

decisions.choice: When he says something, he does it.
decisions.reason: Readable turns the questions into the statements they imply (m3).

decisions.choice: "cambiar de parecer" (L), "cambie de rumbo" (B), "no se echa atrás" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb here means to go back on a decision (meaning decision m2). "Arrepentirse" suggests remorse for wrongdoing, which is not the point, and the doc on recurring terms reserves "cambiar de parecer" for changing one's mind.

decisions.choice: "se raviser" (L), "changer d'avis" (B)
decisions.reason: "Se repentir" in French means remorse for sin; the line says that God does not go back on what he has decided (m2).

decisions.choice: "abadili nia yake" (L), "angebadili mwelekeo" (B), "habadilishi kile alichokwisha kuamua" (R)
decisions.reason: "Kujuta" means to feel regret or remorse; the point is that God does not reverse his decision (m2). Swahili needs no gender span: "mwanadamu" and "binadamu" already mean any human being.

source.text: הִנֵּ֥ה בָרֵ֖ךְ לָקָ֑חְתִּי וּבֵרֵ֖ךְ וְלֹ֥א אֲשִׁיבֶֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, to bless I have received, and he has blessed, and not I can turn it back.

en.L: Look, I have received [a command] to bless; \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has blessed, and I cannot turn it back.
en.B: Look, I was given orders to bless; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has blessed, and I cannot reverse it.
en.R: I was told to bless Israel. \q God has blessed them, and I cannot change that.

es.L: Mira, he recibido [orden de] bendecir; \q y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha bendecido, y no puedo revocarlo.
es.B: Mira, se me ordenó bendecir; \q {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha bendecido, y yo no puedo deshacerlo.
es.R: Recibí la orden de bendecir a Israel. \q Dios los ha bendecido, y yo no puedo cambiar eso.

fr.L: Voici, j’ai reçu [l’ordre] de bénir ; \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a béni, et je ne puis le révoquer.
fr.B: Voici, j’ai reçu l’ordre de bénir ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a béni, et je ne peux pas revenir là-dessus.
fr.R: On m’a demandé de bénir Israël. \q Dieu les a bénis, et je ne peux rien y changer.

sw.L: Tazama, nimepokea [agizo] la kubariki; \q {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} amebariki, wala siwezi kulirudisha.
sw.B: Tazama, nimeagizwa kubariki; \q {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} amebariki, nami siwezi kulibatilisha.
sw.R: Niliambiwa niwabariki Israeli. \q Mungu amewabariki, nami siwezi kubadilisha jambo hilo.

decisions.choice: I have received to bless: I was given a command to bless
decisions.reason: "Received" is used of receiving an order or a charge. Balaam came to curse but was given the task of blessing.

decisions.choice: he has blessed: God is the one who blessed
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "and he has blessed", that is, God. The ancient Greek translation reads "I will bless", which makes Balaam the one who blesses. The Hebrew reading fits verses 8 and 19: what God has blessed no one can undo.

decisions.choice: turn it back: reverse, revoke
decisions.reason: To turn a word back is to cancel it or make it fail. Isaiah 43:13 uses the verb of God's acts: "I act, and who can turn it back?"

decisions.choice: bless Israel ... God has blessed them
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who blessed (m2) and Israel as the people blessed.

source.text: לֹֽא־הִבִּ֥יט אָ֨וֶן֙ בְּיַעֲקֹ֔ב וְלֹא־רָאָ֥ה עָמָ֖ל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהָיו֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וּתְרוּעַ֥ת מֶ֖לֶךְ בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Not has he looked on disaster in Jacob, and not has he seen trouble in Israel; Yahweh his God [is] with him, and [the] shout of a king [is] among him.

en.L: He has not looked on disaster in Jacob, \q nor has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} seen trouble in Israel; \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God [is] with him, \q and the shout of a king [is] among him.
en.B: He sees no disaster for Jacob \q and no trouble for Israel. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} their God is with them, \q and the shout for a king rings out among them.
en.R: God sees no disaster for Jacob's people. \q He sees no trouble for Israel. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} their God is with them. \q They shout for joy to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as their king.

es.L: No ha mirado desgracia en Jacob, \q ni ha visto aflicción en Israel; \q {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} su Dios [está] con él, \q y el clamor de un rey [está] en medio de él.
es.B: No ve desastre para Jacob \q ni aflicción para Israel. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} su Dios está con ellos, \q y entre ellos resuena la aclamación al rey.
es.R: Dios no ve ninguna desgracia para el pueblo de Jacob. \q No ve ningún sufrimiento para Israel. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} su Dios está con ellos. \q Ellos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} aclaman con gritos de alegría como su rey.

fr.L: Il n’a pas regardé le malheur en Jacob, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’a pas vu la peine en Israël ; \q {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} son Dieu [est] avec lui, \q et l’acclamation d’un roi [est] au milieu de lui.
fr.B: Il ne voit pas de malheur pour Jacob \q ni de détresse pour Israël. \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} leur Dieu est avec eux, \q et l’acclamation du roi retentit parmi eux.
fr.R: Dieu ne voit pas de malheur pour le peuple de Jacob. \q Il ne voit pas de souffrance pour Israël. \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} leur Dieu est avec eux. \q Ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}acclament avec des cris de joie comme leur roi.

sw.L: Hakuona msiba katika Yakobo, \q wala hakuona taabu katika Israeli; \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wake [yu] pamoja naye, \q na kelele za [kumshangilia] mfalme [ziko] kati yake.
sw.B: Haoni msiba kwa ajili ya Yakobo, \q wala taabu kwa ajili ya Israeli. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wao yu pamoja nao, \q na shangwe za kumsalimu mfalme zinasikika kati yao.
sw.R: Mungu haoni msiba wowote kwa watu wa Yakobo. \q Haoni taabu yoyote kwa Israeli. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wao yu pamoja nao. \q Wanampigia kelele za furaha kama mfalme wao.

decisions.choice: he has not looked on disaster ... trouble: God sees no harm in store for Israel
alternatives: he has not looked on wrongdoing in Jacob
no one sees disaster in Jacob
decisions.reason: The two nouns can mean wrongdoing and mischief (Psalm 10:7; Habakkuk 1:3) or misfortune and hardship. With the blessing that cannot be reversed (verse 20), the sense is most likely that God sees no disaster coming on Israel. Read the other way, the line says that God does not look on Israel's sin, overlooking it. The subject "he" is probably God, named in the next line; it could also be general: "no one sees disaster in Jacob".

decisions.choice: the shout of a king: the people's shout acclaiming the LORD as their king
decisions.reason: The word is the loud shout raised to hail a king (1 Samuel 10:24) or as a battle cry, and the trumpet blast of the camp (10:5-9). The king is the LORD himself, who reigns over Israel (Exodus 15:18; Deuteronomy 33:5).

decisions.choice: his God ... with him ... among him: Israel as one person
decisions.reason: As in verse 9, Israel is spoken of as "him". "His God" is Israel's God, the LORD.

decisions.choice: their God ... with them ... among them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "they" for the people, as in verse 9.

decisions.choice: God sees ... They shout for joy to him as their king
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who sees (m1) and says plainly that the king being hailed is the LORD (m2).

source.text: אֵ֖ל מוֹצִיאָ֣ם מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם כְּתוֹעֲפֹ֥ת רְאֵ֖ם לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: God [is] bringing them out from Egypt; like [the] horns of a wild ox [are] for him.

en.L: God [is] bringing them out from Egypt; \q like [the] horns of a wild ox [are] for him.
en.B: God brought them out of Egypt; \q they have strength like the horns of a wild ox.
en.R: God brought them out of Egypt. \q They are as strong as a wild ox with its horns.

es.L: Dios [es quien] los saca de Egipto; \q como [los] cuernos de un toro salvaje [son] para él.
es.B: Dios los sacó de Egipto; \q tienen fuerza como los cuernos de un toro salvaje.
es.R: Dios los sacó de Egipto. \q Son tan fuertes como un toro salvaje con sus cuernos.

fr.L: Dieu [est celui qui] les fait sortir d’Égypte ; \q comme [les] cornes d’un taureau sauvage [sont] à lui.
fr.B: Dieu les a fait sortir d’Égypte ; \q ils ont une force pareille aux cornes du taureau sauvage.
fr.R: Dieu les a fait sortir d’Égypte. \q Ils sont aussi forts qu’un taureau sauvage avec ses cornes.

sw.L: Mungu [ndiye] anayewatoa Misri; \q kama pembe za fahali mwitu [ziko] kwake.
sw.B: Mungu aliwatoa Misri; \q wana nguvu kama pembe za fahali mwitu.
sw.R: Mungu aliwatoa Misri. \q Wana nguvu kama fahali mwitu mwenye pembe zake.

decisions.choice: bringing them out: God's act of rescue, which still marks who Israel is
decisions.reason: The verb is a participle, describing God as the one who brings Israel out of Egypt. The exodus happened forty years before, but it remains what God is known by (Exodus 20:2). 24:8 repeats the line.

decisions.choice: the horns of a wild ox: great strength
decisions.reason: The animal is the wild ox (the aurochs), a huge wild bull now extinct, known for its strength and horns (Deuteronomy 33:17; Job 39:9-10). The rare word for "horns" may also mean high peaks or towering strength.

decisions.choice: for him: Israel has the strength of a wild ox
alternatives: he (God) is for them like the horns of a wild ox
decisions.reason: "Him" is most likely Israel: in 24:8, where the line returns, the one with the wild ox's horns goes on to devour the nations. It could also mean that God is like a wild ox's horns for Israel, its strength and defense.

decisions.choice: brought
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "brought", since the rescue from Egypt was past (m1). Literal keeps the participle.

decisions.choice: they have strength like ... / They are as strong as
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the comparison (m2, m3).

decisions.choice: "toro salvaje"
decisions.reason: The animal is the wild ox, the aurochs (m2); "búfalo" names another animal and "unicornio" an old rendering of a legendary one.

decisions.choice: "taureau sauvage"
decisions.reason: The animal is the wild ox, the aurochs (meaning decision m2). "Buffle" names a different animal and "licorne" (an old rendering) a legendary one; "aurochs" is exact but rare, so "taureau sauvage" says it plainly.

decisions.choice: "fahali mwitu"
decisions.reason: "Nyati" is the African buffalo, a different animal; "fahali mwitu" (a wild bull) describes the aurochs (m2).

source.text: כִּ֤י לֹא־נַ֨חַשׁ֙ בְּיַעֲקֹ֔ב וְלֹא־קֶ֖סֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כָּעֵ֗ת יֵאָמֵ֤ר לְיַעֲקֹב֙ וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מַה־פָּ֖עַל אֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: For not [is there] omen in Jacob, and not divination in Israel; at [the] time it will be said of Jacob and of Israel, what has done God!

en.L: For [there is] no omen against Jacob, \q and no divination against Israel; \q now it will be said of Jacob and of Israel, \q 'What God has done!'
en.B: No omen can work against Jacob, \q no divination against Israel. \q Now it will be said of Jacob and of Israel, \q 'See what God has done!'
en.R: No magic sign can harm Jacob's people. \q No fortune-telling can work against Israel. \q Now people will say about Jacob and Israel, \q 'Look at what God has done!'

es.L: Porque no [hay] agüero contra Jacob, \q ni adivinación contra Israel; \q ahora se dirá de Jacob y de Israel: \q “¡Lo que ha hecho Dios!”.
es.B: Ningún agüero puede contra Jacob, \q ninguna adivinación contra Israel. \q Ahora se dirá de Jacob y de Israel: \q “¡Qué obra ha hecho Dios!”.
es.R: Ninguna señal mágica puede dañar al pueblo de Jacob. \q Ninguna adivinación puede obrar contra Israel. \q Ahora la gente dirá de Jacob y de Israel: \q “¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} lo que ha hecho Dios!”.

fr.L: Car [il n’y a] pas de présage contre Jacob, \q et pas de divination contre Israël ; \q maintenant on dira de Jacob et d’Israël : \q “Ce que Dieu a fait !”
fr.B: Aucun présage n’a de pouvoir contre Jacob, \q aucune divination contre Israël. \q Maintenant on dira de Jacob et d’Israël : \q “Voyez ce que Dieu a fait !”
fr.R: Aucun signe magique ne peut faire de mal au peuple de Jacob. \q Aucune voyance ne peut agir contre Israël. \q Maintenant, les gens diront à propos de Jacob et d’Israël : \q “Regardez ce que Dieu a fait !”

sw.L: Kwa maana hakuna ramli juu ya Yakobo, \q wala uaguzi juu ya Israeli; \q sasa itasemwa juu ya Yakobo na juu ya Israeli, \q 'Lo! Aliyoyatenda Mungu!'
sw.B: Hakuna ramli iwezayo kumdhuru Yakobo, \q wala uaguzi dhidi ya Israeli. \q Sasa itasemwa juu ya Yakobo na Israeli, \q 'Tazameni aliyoyatenda Mungu!'
sw.R: Hakuna ishara ya kichawi inayoweza kuwadhuru watu wa Yakobo. \q Hakuna utabiri unaoweza kufanya kazi dhidi ya Israeli. \q Sasa watu watasema juu ya Yakobo na Israeli, \q 'Angalieni mambo aliyoyatenda Mungu!'

decisions.choice: against Jacob: no omen works against Israel
alternatives: there is no omen-reading in Jacob, no divination in Israel
decisions.reason: The small word can mean "in" or "against". Read "against", it says that no spell or omen can harm Israel, which is what Balaam is finding (verses 8, 20). Read "in", it says that Israel does not use omens and divination (Deuteronomy 18:10-15), because God makes his will known to it directly; the next line, about what God has done, can fit either reading.

decisions.choice: omen, divination: ways of seeking hidden knowledge or power
decisions.reason: The first word means reading omens, signs in nature or in a cup (Genesis 44:5; Leviticus 19:26). The second is divination, seeking secret knowledge by lots or other means; Balak's elders had brought Balaam "fees for divination" (22:7). Both were forbidden in Israel (Deuteronomy 18:10). Balaam had been looking for omens (24:1).

decisions.choice: now: at this time
decisions.reason: The phrase means "at the time", that is, now, as in Judges 13:23. Some take it as "in due time", when the story of what God did will be told.

decisions.choice: can work against / can harm
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "can", which states the sense of "against" (m1).

decisions.choice: magic sign, fortune-telling
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for the two practices (m2).

decisions.choice: "agüero" for the first word, "adivinación" for the second
decisions.reason: The first word is reading omens, the second seeking hidden knowledge (meaning decision m2); "agüero" and "adivinación" name the two practices, and "adivinación" matches Balaam's "fees for divination" in chapter 22.

decisions.choice: "présage" for the first word, "divination" for the second
decisions.reason: The first word is reading omens, the second divination (m2); "divination" matches chapter 22, and "présage" keeps the two apart.

decisions.choice: "ramli" for the first word, "uaguzi" for the second
decisions.reason: "Ramli" follows Genesis 44, where the same first word is used of Joseph's cup; "uaguzi" is the word chapter 22 uses for Balaam's divination. "Uchawi" (witchcraft) would say something else.

source.text: הֶן־עָם֙ כְּלָבִ֣יא יָק֔וּם וְכַאֲרִ֖י יִתְנַשָּׂ֑א לֹ֤א יִשְׁכַּב֙ עַד־יֹ֣אכַל טֶ֔רֶף וְדַם־חֲלָלִ֖ים יִשְׁתֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, a people like a lioness rises, and like a lion it lifts itself up; not it will lie down until it eats prey, and [the] blood of slain [ones] it drinks.

en.L: Look, a people rises like a lioness, \q and like a lion it lifts itself up; \q it will not lie down until it eats prey \q and drinks [the] blood of [the] slain."
en.B: Here is a people that rises up like a lioness \q and rouses itself like a lion. \q It does not lie down until it has eaten its prey \q and drunk the blood of the slain."
en.R: These people are like a lioness getting up to hunt. \q They are like a lion ready to attack. \q They will not rest until they have eaten what they caught \q and drunk the blood of those they killed."

es.L: He aquí un pueblo que se levanta como leona, \q y como león se yergue; \q no se echará hasta que coma la presa \q y beba [la] sangre de [los] muertos».
es.B: He aquí un pueblo que se alza como una leona \q y se yergue como un león. \q No se echa hasta haber devorado su presa \q y bebido la sangre de sus víctimas».
es.R: Este pueblo es como una leona que se levanta para cazar. \q Es como un león listo para atacar. \q No descansará hasta comerse lo que ha cazado \q y beber la sangre de los que ha matado».

fr.L: Voici, un peuple se lève comme une lionne, \q et comme un lion il se dresse ; \q il ne se couchera pas qu’il n’ait mangé la proie \q et bu [le] sang des tués. »
fr.B: Voici un peuple qui se lève comme une lionne \q et se dresse comme un lion. \q Il ne se couche pas avant d’avoir dévoré sa proie \q et bu le sang de ses victimes. »
fr.R: Ce peuple est comme une lionne qui se lève pour chasser. \q Il est comme un lion prêt à attaquer. \q Il ne se reposera pas avant d’avoir mangé ce qu’il a attrapé \q et bu le sang de ceux qu’il a tués. »

sw.L: Tazama, watu wanaoinuka kama simba jike, \q na kama simba wanajiinua; \q hawatalala mpaka wale mawindo \q na kunywa damu ya waliouawa."
sw.B: Hawa ni watu wanaoinuka kama simba jike, \q na kujiinua kama simba. \q Hawalali mpaka wamekula mawindo yao \q na kunywa damu ya waliouawa."
sw.R: Watu hawa ni kama simba jike anayeamka kwenda kuwinda. \q Ni kama simba aliye tayari kushambulia. \q Hawatapumzika mpaka wamekula walichokamata \q na kunywa damu ya wale waliowaua."

decisions.choice: a lioness ... a lion: Israel pictured as a lion, as in Jacob's blessing
decisions.reason: Hebrew has several words for lions; the first here may mean a lioness, the hunter of the pride. The same pair describes Judah in Jacob's blessing (Genesis 49:9), and Balaam uses it again in 24:9.

decisions.choice: not lie down until it eats prey: Israel will defeat its enemies
decisions.reason: A lion does not rest until it has fed. The picture is of Israel's victory in war, as over Sihon and Og just before (21:21-35).

decisions.choice: getting up to hunt / ready to attack
decisions.reason: Readable says why the lion rises: to hunt, as the following lines show (m2).

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בָּלָק֙ אֶל־בִּלְעָ֔ם גַּם־קֹ֖ב לֹ֣א תִקֳּבֶ֑נּוּ גַּם־בָּרֵ֖ךְ לֹ֥א תְבָרֲכֶֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Balak to Balaam, neither cursing will you curse it, nor blessing will you bless it.

en.L: And Balak said to Balaam, "Neither curse it at all, nor bless it at all!"
en.B: Then Balak said to Balaam, "Do not curse them at all, and do not bless them at all!"
en.R: Then Balak said to Balaam, "Do not curse them, then, but do not bless them either!"

es.L: Y dijo Balac a Balaam: «¡Ni le eches maldición alguna, ni lo bendigas en absoluto!».
es.B: Entonces Balac dijo a Balaam: «¡No les eches ninguna maldición, pero tampoco los bendigas en absoluto!».
es.R: Entonces Balac le dijo a Balaam: «¡Pues no los maldigas, pero tampoco los bendigas!».

fr.L: Et Balak dit à Balaam : « Ne lance pas du tout de malédiction contre lui, et ne le bénis pas du tout non plus ! »
fr.B: Alors Balak dit à Balaam : « Ne lance aucune malédiction contre eux, mais ne les bénis pas non plus ! »
fr.R: Alors Balak a dit à Balaam : « Bon, ne les maudis pas, mais ne les bénis pas non plus ! »

sw.L: Naye Balaki akamwambia Balaamu, "Usimwapize kabisa, wala usimbariki kabisa!"
sw.B: Kisha Balaki akamwambia Balaamu, "Usiwaapize hata kidogo, wala usiwabariki hata kidogo!"
sw.R: Kisha Balaki akamwambia Balaamu, "Basi usiwalaani, lakini usiwabariki pia!"

decisions.choice: neither curse it at all, nor bless it at all: if not a curse, at least no more blessing
decisions.reason: Each verb is doubled for emphasis, and "neither ... nor" joins the two commands. Balak gives up hope of a curse from this place and wants at least to stop the blessings. "It" is the people of Israel, as in verse 13.

decisions.choice: them
decisions.reason: As in verse 13, Balanced and Readable say "them" for the people.

source.text: וַיַּ֣עַן בִּלְעָ֔ם וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֶל־בָּלָ֑ק הֲלֹ֗א דִּבַּ֤רְתִּי אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־יְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֹת֥וֹ אֶֽעֱשֶֽׂה׃
